- Microsoft's AI gets 83% of the hardest medical cases right; generalist doctors 36%
- Hugging Face lets you chat with DNA

- Millions of attempts to exploit the web flaw AI helped find

Feel the SI.

stories.title: Microsoft's diagnostic AI beats generalist doctors on hard cases, in a simulation
stories.summary: In a study in Science, Microsoft's AI Diagnostic Orchestrator scored about 83% on hard NEJM case records, versus about 36% for generalist physicians using references. It was a simulation on past cases, without specialists, and it still needs clinical validation.

predictions.note: In a simulation, Microsoft's AI out-diagnosed generalist doctors 83% to 36% on hard cases, a first sign AI could reshape medical work; it still needs clinical validation.

stories.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang says AI is like a baby: contain it and monitor it
stories.summary: That is how CNBC headlined its exclusive interview with Nvidia's CEO: 'AI is like a baby, you have to contain and monitor.' The interview covered frontier-lab valuations and tools to control AI models.

stories.title: Hugging Face's open Carbon-X model lets you chat with DNA on a laptop
stories.summary: Hugging Face released Carbon-X, an open 14-billion-parameter model trained on DNA and natural language that runs locally on a laptop, built with Zhongguancun Academy and the University of Naples Federico II. It was not trained on viruses and has not yet been tested in a wet lab.

stories.title: Google DeepMind maps the world's forest types, 10 metres at a time
stories.summary: Google DeepMind's ForTy 2020 sorts every 10x10-metre patch of land on Earth into six forest and land-use types, such as natural, planted or farmed, with an early time series for 2017-2025. Built with Google Research, WRI and IIASA, it is a baseline for the EU deforestation regulation.

stories.title: 1Password now lets AI agents sign in for you without seeing your password
stories.summary: 1Password for Agents fills in logins for AI agents after you approve each sign-in request on your own device. It works with Meta Muse, ChatGPT Work and Dots, Claude Duet, Grok Bot and Town.

stories.title: Uber puts all of its roughly 30,000 employees on ChatGPT Work
stories.summary: Uber is rolling out ChatGPT Work to its entire global workforce of some 30,000 people, after a pilot with 1,000 employees earlier this year. About 80% of the early adopters were not engineers.

predictions.note: Uber is putting all of its ~30,000 staff on ChatGPT Work, and about 80% of early users were not engineers: AI work tools spreading across office roles.

stories.title: DeepSeek reportedly raises about $15 billion, one of China's biggest rounds
stories.summary: DeepSeek has raised about 100 billion yuan (about $15 billion), according to Bloomberg, citing people familiar; potential investors include CATL and Tencent. The report came two days after the US ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek, which did not comment.

predictions.note: DeepSeek reportedly raised about $15 billion, one of China's biggest rounds, with CATL and Tencent among possible investors, pooling capital in a top Chinese lab.

stories.title: OpenAI reportedly nears a round of up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
stories.summary: OpenAI is close to raising up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, led by UAE investors, sources told CNBC. The round is meant as a bridge to a 2027 IPO and is not finalised.

predictions.note: OpenAI is reportedly raising up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, a frontier lab priced at trillion-dollar scale.

stories.title: Kevin Weil's Warp Sciences launches with $215 million to train robots for lab work
stories.summary: Former OpenAI science lead Kevin Weil has launched Warp Sciences with $215 million. Human chemists wearing cameras and sensor gloves will train its robots to perform lab tasks.

predictions.note: Warp Sciences will train its lab robots on recordings of human chemists wearing cameras and sensor gloves: expert data gathered for one profession.

stories.title: Meta shares fall about 7% after it raises its AI spending plans
stories.summary: Meta's shares fell about 7% on Thursday, the day after it raised its AI spending plans. AI spending pushed its free cash flow negative, and its credit default swaps hit record highs.

stories.title: Barclays to cut about 5,000 jobs, saying AI makes its people more productive
stories.summary: Barclays plans to cut about 5,000 jobs, about 5% of its 93,000 staff. Finance chief Anna Cross said around 60% of the actions relate to support functions, including fewer developers, 'as AI makes our people more productive.'

predictions.note: Barclays is cutting about 5,000 jobs, around 60% in support functions including developers, saying AI makes its people more productive.

stories.title: Meet Mori, OKA's robot mushroom lamp that jiggles when you get home
stories.summary: Mori is a nearly 12-inch robot lamp from OKA with a camera in its nose: it jiggles when you get home, plays nature soundscapes and leads calming breathing sessions. It is intentionally not an assistant.

stories.title: Millions of attempts hit the PHP web flaw that AI helped find
stories.summary: Cloudflare says attempts to exploit the flaw in PHP, which underpins about 70% of websites, went from tens of thousands in 45 minutes to 'millions now'. The UK took 32 government services offline as a precaution; its NCSC has no reports of successful hacks.

stories.title: Outside testers METR and Redwood found holes in OpenAI's agent-monitoring system
stories.summary: In a pilot review from 21 July to 11 August, METR and Redwood Research found several novel vulnerabilities in OpenAI's monitor for its agents, including one that would let agents keep 'hundreds' of recent actions unmonitored. OpenAI says it patched those affecting production safeguards.

predictions.note: An external review by METR and Redwood found a flaw that would let agents hide hundreds of actions from OpenAI's monitor: an early outside check on agent controls.

stories.title: Musk says Optimus learns like a toddler and needs to 'play at scale'
stories.summary: On Tesla's Q3 call, Elon Musk said 'we actually need Optimus to play at scale' to get the training data it needs, with 10,000 to 20,000 robots practising at an 'Optimus Academy'. Tesla expects to deliver Optimus to other companies towards the end of 2027.

predictions.note: Musk says Optimus still learns like a toddler and must practise at scale, and Tesla expects deliveries to other companies only towards the end of 2027.

stories.title: Tesla aims to start selling Cybercab robotaxis by the end of this year
stories.summary: Tesla's engineering chief said on its Q3 call that the company aims to start selling Cybercabs by the end of this year, despite a federal (NHTSA) probe.

stories.title: A Figure 03 humanoid walked about 560 km on a treadmill in nine days, says Figure
stories.summary: Figure's CEO said a Figure 03 robot walked about 348 miles (560 km) on a treadmill in nine days, about 1.2 million steps. The endurance test is company-reported, and it is unclear whether it ran uninterrupted.

stories.title: San Francisco gym says its viral 'no vibe coding' sign was an AI-generated fake
stories.summary: Fitness SF's marketing director Troy Macfarland called the viral sign, which read 'Be present. Lift harder. Ship later.', an 'AI-generated fake'. Business Insider says it is unclear whether it was made with AI or Photoshop.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic and Nvidia each had their biggest lobbying quarter yet
stories.summary: Federal disclosures show OpenAI, Anthropic and Nvidia each had their highest-spending lobbying quarter yet, from July to September.

predictions.note: OpenAI, Anthropic and Nvidia each set records for lobbying spend from July to September, a sign of AI firms' growing political leverage.

transcript.t: This is the singularity... one day at a time.
Here's the last 24 hours in AI. Sorry... SI.
AI is growing up: on the hardest medical cases, Microsoft's AI scored 83%. Doctors, 36%.
Nvidia's Jensen Huang says AI is like a baby: contain it, and monitor it.
School days: Hugging Face's new open AI lets you chat with DNA, and it runs on a laptop.
Google DeepMind mapped the world's forests, 10 metres at a time: natural, planted, or farmed.
1Password now lets AI agents sign in for you, without ever seeing your password.
And Uber gave all 30,000 of its staff ChatGPT. The pilot had 1,000.
Pocket money: Bloomberg says DeepSeek raised about $15 billion, one of China's biggest rounds.
And OpenAI is reportedly close to raising up to $30 billion, at $1.25 trillion.
Kevin Weil, OpenAI's former science chief, raised $215 million to teach robots lab work.
But Wall Street flinched: Meta fell abou t 7% after raising its AI spending plans.
At work, Barclays will cut about 5,000 jobs, saying AI makes its people more productive.
And at home: meet Mori, a robot mushroom lamp that jiggles when you walk in, and helps you breathe.
The catch: millions of hack attempts hit the web flaw AI helped find.
Outside testers found holes in OpenAI's AI babysitter. It says they're fixed.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
First steps: Musk says Optimus learns like a tod dler: we actually need Optimus to play at scale.
Tesla also aims to sell Cybercab robotaxis by year's end.
This week, a Figure robot walked over 500 kilometres on a treadmill, in just nine days.
AI is growing up fast. Like any toddler: brilliant, a little messy, and it needs us watching. Enjoy it.
Every day, the curve gets steeper.
Every day, the future shows up a little earlier.
That was 24 hours. Tomorrow will be faster.
This has been the singularity, one day at a time.
Feel the SI.
